title: Exception Filters: @Catch(), HttpException Normalization, and Error Boundaries

progressiveExplaining.eli5: When a computer program crashes unexpectedly, it usually vomits an ugly stack trace. An Exception Filter is an emergency triage team: it catches any error before it leaves the building, translates it into a polite JSON message with an error code, and logs the crash safely.
progressiveExplaining.junior: Exception Filters catch unhandled exceptions across your application. Create one with `@Catch()` implementing `ExceptionFilter`: `catch(exception, host: ArgumentsHost)`. You extract `const ctx = host.switchToHttp()`, get `response` and `request`, and format a custom error response: `response.status(status).json({ ... })`. NestJS includes built-in classes like `NotFoundException`, `BadRequestException`, and `UnauthorizedException` inheriting from `HttpException`.
progressiveExplaining.senior: Architecturally, Exception Filters provide centralized, transport-agnostic error normalization. Unhandled domain errors (like TypeORM `QueryFailedError` or Prisma `P2002` unique constraint violations) are intercepted before leaking database schemas or internal stack traces to the public internet. Binding `@Catch()` with no arguments creates an **All-Exceptions Filter** acting as the ultimate boundary for both recognized `HttpException`s and unexpected `Error` instances.
progressiveExplaining.underTheHood: When an error is thrown during pipeline execution, NestJS catches it in an internal `try/catch` wrapper and passes it to the `ExceptionsHandler`. The handler searches registered filters (method -> controller -> global). It invokes `filter.catch(exception, host)`. If no custom filter handles the error, NestJS's `BaseExceptionFilter` formats a default JSON response (`statusCode: 500`, `message: 'Internal server error'`).

rosettaStone.express: Express 4-parameter error middleware `(err, req, res, next)`.

codeComparison.title: Try-Catch Controller Boilerplate vs Centralized Exception Filter
codeComparison.summary: Writing try/catch blocks in every controller leaks implementation details; an Exception Filter normalizes errors globally.

legacyOrBad.label: Manual Try-Catch in Controllers
legacyOrBad.snippet: try { await service.find(); } catch (err) { res.status(500).json({ err }); } // ❌ Leaks raw errors

modernOrGood.label: Global All-Exceptions Filter
modernOrGood.snippet: @Catch() export class AllExceptionsFilter implements ExceptionFilter { ... } // ✅ NEW: Centralized & sanitized

interviewGotchas.question: How do you bind an Exception Filter globally while still allowing Dependency Injection (e.g. injecting `ConfigService` or a `Logger`)?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Interviewers test your knowledge of global provider tokens vs `app.useGlobalFilters()`.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer:
Register the filter in `AppModule` using the **`APP_FILTER`** token:
```typescript
{ provide: APP_FILTER, useClass: AllExceptionsFilter }
```
This ensures the filter is managed by the NestJS IoC container with full dependency injection support. Using `app.useGlobalFilters(new AllExceptionsFilter())` in `main.ts` prevents constructor dependency injection.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: Never use `new Filter()` in `main.ts` if your filter requires injected services.

interviewGotchas.question: What is the difference between `@Catch(HttpException)` and `@Catch()` with no arguments?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Checks precision regarding exception inheritance filtering.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: `@Catch(HttpException)` will **only catch exceptions that inherit from `HttpException`** (like `NotFoundException`, `BadRequestException`). Unhandled native errors (e.g. `TypeError`, `DatabaseConnectionError`) will bypass the filter. `@Catch()` (with no arguments) acts as an **All-Exceptions catch-all** that intercepts every single error thrown in the app.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: If using `@Catch(HttpException)`, unhandled database crashes will bypass your filter and be handled by the default fallback.
